abstract.title: Design of Real-Time Energy Forecasting and Carbon Accounting System for Petrochemical Units Using Virtual Sample Generation
abstract.text: Petrochemical plants face regulatory pressure to reduce emissions while limited training data hinders forecasting model development. This paper presents design of intelligent system addressing small data problem through virtual sample generation (Monte Carlo, Particle Swarm Optimization). System architecture integrates real-time data acquisition via OPC-UA, machine learning (ELM, LSTM) for 60-minute energy forecasting, comprehensive Scope 1/2/3 carbon accounting using IPCC factors. Design targets olefin and PTA units. System at TRL 3-4; results pending validation on real plant data. Work documents system architecture and design methodology rather than field-validated performance. Design target for prediction error is MAPE below 5% (requirement specification, not measured result).

abstract.title: Multi-Mode Adaptive Decision System for UAV Missions: Design and Simulation Study
abstract.text: Autonomous UAV missions require real-time mode selection (reconnaissance, surveillance, pursuit, loiter, return, engagement) based on dynamic conditions. This paper presents design of adaptive decision system evaluating six modes using weighted multi-criteria scoring at 10 Hz targeting STM32H7 hardware. Design addresses multi-objective optimization balancing energy, mission success, survival under resource constraints. Design target: decision latency below 5ms, mode accuracy target above 90% per requirements. Environmental factors and mission priority dynamically adjust weights. System at TRL 3; assessment on 400 simulated scenarios with no actual flight data. Work documents decision architecture and methodology for future flight validation.

abstract.title: AI-Based Optimization of Gas, Chemical, and Steam Injection for Enhanced Oil Recovery: Reservoir Simulation Design Study
abstract.text: Enhanced oil recovery through gas/chemical/steam injection requires optimization balancing recovery and costs. This paper presents design of AI system combining reservoir behavior prediction (Deep Neural Networks) with injection parameter optimization. Design addresses real-time injection control for maximizing recovery while minimizing operational costs. System targets oil reservoir applications. At TRL 3-4; assessment on simulated reservoir data with no real field data. Work documents system architecture and optimization methodology. Design targets: recovery increase 12-15% over baseline (design target from case studies, not measured), cost reduction 20-30% through optimization (design target). Validation on real reservoir and field pilot data required.

abstract.title: Predictive Monitoring of Reformer Tube Creep and Methanol Catalyst Degradation: Generic Methods for Natural Gas to Methanol Plants
abstract.text: Natural gas to methanol plants face reformer tube creep risk (catastrophic rupture) and methanol catalyst sintering (activity loss). Existing methods rely on periodic inspection; real-time prediction rare. This paper presents design of digital twin system predicting remaining creep life and catalyst degradation from continuous DCS data (tube skin temperature, stress, reactor conditions). Methods described generically suitable for any single-train methanol plant. Design targets: creep life prediction accuracy MAPE below 15% (design specification), catalyst trend correlation above 0.90 (design target), early warnings 48-72h before critical thresholds. System at TRL 3; assessment on simulated plant data with no real validation. Work documents predictive monitoring methodology without disclosing client-specific information.
